proposals.evidence: DEDR 2626 gives Gondi sīṛ/sīr, hīr and īr ‘root’; the two survey responses match the printed h-initial and zero-initial variants. Its Maithili sīr cross-reference leaves regional contact open; this proposal follows the attested Dravidian lexical grouping without inventing a donor route.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4035 explicitly lists Gondi pīni and Parji pañil ‘cold’, alongside Tamil paṉi ‘cold; dew’. The complete local forms and cold sense agree, including the Parji final -l; the survey gloss is not converted to dew or fever.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5086 gives Kannada mēle ‘above, top’ and explicitly distinguishes Maria Gondi mēlo ‘bad’ from Koya mēlta ‘good’ and mēlo ‘taboo’ in another source. The Bhamani Madia survey’s melo ‘bad’ follows the Maria attestation; its meaning is preserved rather than inferred from the opposite Koya sense.
